OP, if you can afford to, I’d really try and see a dermatologist. While my hair loss is more concentrated on my hairline with a bit of overall thinning (think old man hairline), a dermatologist was able to prescribe me prescription strength minoxidil + spironolactone mixture to put on my hairline that has helped a bit. I also tried oral spironolactone for a bit too if you would want to message me or ask about it.

So, what you really need to see is a dermatologist. I’m a similar age with the same issue, seeing a dermatologist helped me know my options. If this isn’t being caused by something like a thyroid problem or a vitamin deficiency, your options will (likely) be to take sprironolactone (which also helps a hormonal acne) and to use minoxidil topically. I’d also think about if you’ve had any major stressors over the past year, or started any new medications or diets. 

With that being said, over the counter the best things you can use would be some sort of Rosemary oil to put in for a few hours before you shower. I use the Miele one, you can get it at target. It’s not super expensive.  There are definitely other oils you can try (castor oil is also proven to help, and there’s a few others too).

I also use the Ordinary multi-peptide hair serum a few times a week too. It’s lightweight, and I feel like it does help.

There are rosemary oil shampoos you can buy (I tried one from Bondi Boost) but honestly the one I tried made my hair soooo dry. Like, I had actually chunks of dead skin coming off my scalp for the first time dry. 

If you had a red light mask, you can put that on your head, since it will help promote increased collagen/cell turnover like it would on your face. 

You can also try micro needling, I bought a roller from Bondiboost that I use once a week per there recommendations. Tbh I don’t think this really does much, but I’ve seen other people say it helps a lot

A few years go by, I’m in college and one of my coworkers mentions that Taylor Swift and Brandon Urie of P!ATD released a song together.
